extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: A fully authentic visual question answering dataset sourced from online question answering communities, where each example includes a natural language question, image, context, and an accepted answer validated by the individual asking the question.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping publicly available Stack Exchange data and collecting examples containing a natural language question, natural language context, an image, and at least one answer. The original content came from Stack Exchange user interactions, and only examples with an accepted answer were retained.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Examples whose images could not be downloaded from the provided link were removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public Stack Exchange archive data in XML format, including post titles, body text, image URL links, answers, accepted-answer markers, scores, and topic-site information.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were converted to PNG format for consistency, and training/validation splits were created by random selection per topic.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors filtered candidate visual questions by requiring an accepted answer, removing low-quality posts with question or answer scores of 0 or less, excluding examples with multiple images or visual answers, removing examples whose images could not be downloaded, and converting images to PNG format.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Topic labels come from authentic user-chosen Stack Exchange topical sites. Additional user-intention annotations were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk: three crowdworkers labeled one primary intent per visual question for 105 randomly selected VQAs, with two independent annotations per item and a third worker used to break ties. The final label was assigned by majority vote.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk; spreadsheet-based annotation workflow
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The user-intention taxonomy was refined through four rounds of annotator analysis by two author-annotators, with disagreements discussed and resolved and definitions adjusted accordingly. Agreement improved from 53.3% to 87.5%, and Cohen’s kappa improved from 45.24% to 84.69%. Final user-intention labels were assigned by majority vote across three crowdworker annotations when needed.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For crowdworkers: workers located in the United States with more than 500 completed HITs and over a 95% approval rating. For human evaluation annotators: ten domain experts, each assigned one of ten topics, each with at least a Master’s degree in a related field, and located in the United States.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Geography/language-related information may be present; the paper explicitly discusses multilingual VQAs and unbalanced geographic representation of Stack Exchange users.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset may support improved VQA models for real-world applications such as community question answering platforms, learning assistance tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog/query, and visual search/browsing. The paper also notes underrepresentation of people in poverty-stricken areas and geographic imbalance in Stack Exchange users.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas because it is limited to Stack Exchange users with internet and mobile-device access, and geographic representation is unbalanced with more users from the US, India, and Europe and fewer from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may underrepresent people in poverty-stricken areas and has geographically unbalanced representation. The paper also notes that many benchmarked models may have seen Stack Exchange data during training, creating potential data contamination for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset supports few-shot learning and includes training, validation, and test splits. It is used for benchmarking and evaluating VQA models, especially for authentic-use-case VQA with long-form answers.
